<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<title>Give Yourself Grace — Workbook</title>
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lora:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;1,400;1,500;1,600&family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
/* ── Reset & tokens ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
:root {
  --bg:        #F3F6F5;
  --slate:     #2C3A47;
  --slate-lt:  #4A6070;
  --amber:     #D4A373;
  --amber-lt:  #EDD5B3;
  --amber-bg:  #FBF3E8;
  --amber-b2:  #F0E0C4;
  --amber-b3:  #E8CEAA;
  --sage:      #7A9E8E;
  --sage-lt:   #B2CBBF;
  --cream:     #F9F7F1;
  --white:     #FFFFFF;
  --grey:      #8A9BAA;
  --sidebar-w: 280px;
  --content-max: 760px;
  --radius:    10px;
  --shadow:    0 2px 12px rgba(44,58,71,.08);
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.65;
}

/* ── Typography ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
body {
  font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif;
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--slate);
  min-height: 100vh;
}
h1,h2,h3,h4 { font-family: 'Lora', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; }
p { margin-bottom: .85em; }

/* ── Layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.layout { display: flex; min-height: 100vh; }

/* Sidebar */
.sidebar {
  width: var(--sidebar-w);
  background: var(--slate);
  color: var(--cream);
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; height: 100vh;
  overflow-y: auto; overflow-x: hidden;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  z-index: 100;
  transition: transform .3s ease;
  scrollbar-width: thin;
  scrollbar-color: var(--amber) var(--slate);
}
.sidebar-logo {
  padding: 28px 24px 20px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(212,163,115,.25);
}
.sidebar-logo img { width: 130px; filter: brightness(0) invert(1); opacity: .9; }
.sidebar-nav { padding: 16px 0 32px; flex: 1; }
.sidebar-nav h4 {
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--amber-lt); padding: 0 24px 10px;
}
.sidebar-nav ul { list-style: none; }
.sidebar-nav li a {
  display: block; padding: 9px 24px;
  color: rgba(249,247,241,.75); text-decoration: none;
  font-size: 13px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.4;
  border-left: 3px solid transparent;
  transition: all .18s ease;
}
.sidebar-nav li a:hover,
.sidebar-nav li a.active {
  color: var(--amber-lt);
  border-left-color: var(--amber);
  background: rgba(212,163,115,.10);
  padding-left: 28px;
}
.sidebar-progress {
  padding: 20px 24px 28px;
  border-top: 1px solid rgba(212,163,115,.2);
}
.progress-label { font-size: 11px; color: var(--amber-lt); margin-bottom: 8px; letter-spacing: .05em; }
.progress-bar { background: rgba(255,255,255,.15); border-radius: 99px; height: 6px; overflow: hidden; }
.progress-fill { background: var(--amber); height: 100%; border-radius: 99px; width: 0%; transition: width .4s ease; }
.progress-pct { font-size: 11px; color: var(--grey); margin-top: 6px; }

/* Main content area */
.main {
  margin-left: var(--sidebar-w);
  flex: 1;
  padding: 0 32px 80px;
  max-width: calc(var(--sidebar-w) + var(--content-max) + 64px);
}

/* ── Cover ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.cover-section {
  min-height: 100vh;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  text-align: center;
  padding: 60px 40px;
  background: linear-gradient(160deg, var(--bg) 0%, #EDE8DC 100%);
  border-bottom: 3px solid var(--amber);
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.cover-section::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute; inset: 0;
  background: radial-gradient(ellipse 60% 50% at 50% 55%, rgba(212,163,115,.18) 0%, transparent 70%);
  pointer-events: none;
}
.cover-title {
  font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 5vw, 4rem);
  letter-spacing: .08em;
  color: var(--slate);
  font-weight: 700;
  margin-bottom: 0;
}
.cover-grace {
  font-size: clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5.5rem);
  font-weight: 700; font-style: italic;
  color: var(--amber);
  text-shadow: 2px 3px 0 rgba(180,130,80,.3);
  line-height: 1.1;
  margin-bottom: 8px;
}
.cover-rule { width: 260px; height: 3px; background: var(--amber); margin: 18px auto 24px; border-radius: 2px; }
.cover-figure {
  width: min(380px, 80vw);
  border-radius: 16px;
  box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(44,58,71,.15);
  margin: 0 auto 28px;
  display: block;
}
.cover-sub {
  font-size: 1.05rem; color: var(--slate-lt);
  max-width: 460px; margin: 0 auto 10px;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 400;
}
.cover-tag {
  font-family: 'Lora', serif; font-style: italic;
  color: var(--sage); font-size: .95rem;
  margin-bottom: 28px;
}
.cover-logo { width: 140px; opacity: .85; }
.cover-border {
  position: absolute; inset: 20px;
  border: 2px solid var(--amber);
  border-radius: 12px;
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* ── Chapter structure ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.chapter {
  max-width: var(--content-max);
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 60px 0 20px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--amber-lt);
}
.chapter:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
.chapter-header { margin-bottom: 32px; }
.chapter-eyebrow {
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--amber); display: block; margin-bottom: 10px;
}
.chapter-title {
  font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 3.5vw, 2.1rem);
  color: var(--slate); margin-bottom: 16px; line-height: 1.25;
}
.amber-rule { height: 2px; background: var(--amber); border-radius: 2px; width: 100%; }
.chapter-content { padding: 8px 0 0; }

/* ── Content typography ───────────────────────────────────────────── */
.chapter-content p {
  font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.7;
  color: var(--slate); margin-bottom: 1rem;
}
.section-h2 {
  font-size: 1.15rem; color: var(--slate);
  margin: 28px 0 10px; padding-bottom: 6px;
  border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--amber-lt);
}
.step-item {
  display: flex; gap: 14px; align-items: flex-start;
  margin: 14px 0; padding: 14px 18px;
  background: var(--cream); border-radius: var(--radius);
  border-left: 3px solid var(--amber);
}
.step-num {
  background: var(--amber); color: white;
  font-family: 'Lora', serif; font-weight: 700;
  width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 50%;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  font-size: .85rem; flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 2px;
}
.step-dot { color: var(--amber); font-size: 1.4rem; line-height: 1; flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 2px; }
.step-body strong { display: block; color: var(--slate); margin-bottom: 4px; font-family: 'Inter'; font-weight: 600; font-size: .95rem; }
.step-body p { margin: 0; font-size: .93rem; color: var(--slate-lt); line-height: 1.6; }
.bullet-item {
  display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: flex-start;
  margin: 8px 0;
}
.bullet-dot { color: var(--amber); font-size: 1.2rem; flex-shrink: 0; line-height: 1.5; }
.bullet-item p { margin: 0; font-size: .97rem; line-height: 1.65; }
.barrier-item {
  display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: baseline;
  margin: 10px 0; padding: 10px 14px;
  background: var(--amber-bg); border-radius: 8px;
}
.barrier-label {
  font-weight: 600; color: var(--slate); white-space: nowrap;
  font-size: .9rem; min-width: 140px;
}
.barrier-item p { margin: 0; font-size: .92rem; color: var(--slate-lt); }

/* ── Note boxes (open writing area) ──────────────────────────────── */
.note-box { margin: 18px 0; }
.note-box-label {
  display: block; font-size: .88rem; font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--slate-lt); margin-bottom: 6px;
}
.note-area, .response-area, .notes-area, .numlist-input {
  width: 100%;
  background: var(--amber-bg);
  border: 1.5px solid var(--amber);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  padding: 14px 16px;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  font-size: .97rem; color: var(--slate);
  line-height: 1.65;
  resize: vertical;
  transition: border-color .18s, box-shadow .18s;
  outline: none;
}
.note-area:focus, .response-area:focus, .notes-area:focus, .numlist-input:focus {
  border-color: var(--sage);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(122,158,142,.18);
}
.note-area::placeholder, .response-area::placeholder, .notes-area::placeholder {
  color: var(--amber-b3); font-style: italic; font-size: .9rem;
}
.numlist-input {
  border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px;
  border-color: var(--amber-lt); resize: none;
}

/* ── Numbered resource list ───────────────────────────────────────── */
.numlist { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; margin: 12px 0; }
.numlist-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
.numlist-n { font-weight: 600; color: var(--amber); min-width: 26px; font-size: .9rem; }
.numlist-input { flex: 1; }

/* ── Deliberations ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.deliberations-section {
  margin-top: 48px;
  padding-top: 40px;
  border-top: 2px dashed var(--amber-lt);
}
.deli-header { margin-bottom: 28px; }
.deli-eyebrow {
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 10px;
  font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--amber); display: block; margin-bottom: 8px;
}
.deli-title {
  font-size: 1.25rem; color: var(--slate);
  margin-bottom: 14px; letter-spacing: .04em;
}
.slate-rule { height: 2.5px; background: var(--slate); border-radius: 2px; }
.deli-content { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 18px; padding-top: 8px; }

/* ── Question blocks ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.question-block { border-radius: var(--radius); overflow: hidden; box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
.question-header {
  background: var(--amber-b2);
  padding: 14px 18px 12px;
  border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--amber);
}
.question-label {
  display: block;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 600;
  font-size: .97rem; color: var(--slate);
  margin-bottom: 5px;
}
.question-prompt {
  font-size: .88rem; color: var(--slate-lt);
  line-height: 1.55; margin: 0;
}
.response-area {
  display: block;
  border-radius: 0 0 var(--radius) var(--radius);
  border-top: none;
}

/* ── Notes pages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.notes-page {
  margin: 32px 0;
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  border: 1.5px solid var(--amber);
  overflow: hidden;
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
.notes-page-header {
  background: var(--amber-b2);
  padding: 14px 20px 12px;
  border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--amber);
}
.notes-page-num {
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 600;
  font-size: .8rem; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--amber); display: block; margin-bottom: 4px;
}
.notes-page-sub { font-size: .85rem; color: var(--slate-lt); margin: 0; font-style: italic; }
.notes-area { border-radius: 0; border: none; border-top: none; min-height: 340px; }

/* ── Intro section ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#intro {
  max-width: var(--content-max);
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 60px 0 20px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--amber-lt);
}
.intro-quote {
  font-family: 'Lora', serif; font-style: italic;
  font-size: 1.1rem; color: var(--sage);
  border-left: 3px solid var(--amber);
  padding: 14px 20px; margin: 24px 0;
  background: var(--amber-bg); border-radius: 0 8px 8px 0;
  line-height: 1.7;
}

/* ── Closing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.closing {
  max-width: var(--content-max);
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 80px 0 60px;
  text-align: center;
}
.closing-logo { width: 160px; margin: 0 auto 32px; display: block; }
.closing-rule { width: 200px; height: 2px; background: var(--amber); margin: 24px auto; border-radius: 2px; }
.closing h2 { font-size: 2rem; margin-bottom: 10px; color: var(--slate); }
.closing-sub { font-size: 1.25rem; font-style: italic; color: var(--slate-lt); margin-bottom: 24px; }
.closing-tag {
  font-family: 'Lora', serif; font-style: italic;
  color: var(--sage); font-size: 1rem; max-width: 420px; margin: 0 auto;
  line-height: 1.7;
}

/* ── TOC (progress nav) ───────────────────────────────────────────── */
.toc-section {
  max-width: var(--content-max); margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 60px 0 20px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--amber-lt);
}
.toc-section h2 { font-size: 1.8rem; margin-bottom: 20px; }
.toc-list { list-style: none; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.toc-list li a {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
  padding: 11px 16px; border-radius: 8px;
  text-decoration: none; color: var(--slate);
  font-size: .95rem; transition: background .15s;
}
.toc-list li:nth-child(odd) a { background: var(--amber-bg); }
.toc-list li:nth-child(even) a { background: var(--cream); }
.toc-list li a:hover { background: var(--amber-b2); }
.toc-list li a .toc-num {
  min-width: 28px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--amber);
  font-family: 'Lora', serif;
}

/* ── Mobile sidebar toggle ────────────────────────────────────────── */
.menu-toggle {
  display: none;
  position: fixed; top: 16px; left: 16px; z-index: 200;
  background: var(--slate); color: var(--amber-lt);
  border: none; border-radius: 8px;
  width: 42px; height: 42px; cursor: pointer;
  font-size: 1.3rem; box-shadow: 0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.2);
}
.sidebar-overlay {
  display: none;
  position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0,0,0,.5);
  z-index: 90;
}

/* ── Print styles ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
@media print {
  .sidebar, .menu-toggle { display: none !important; }
  .main { margin-left: 0; max-width: 100%; padding: 0 24px; }
  .chapter { page-break-before: always; padding-top: 32px; }
  .question-block { page-break-inside: avoid; }
  .response-area { min-height: 120px; }
  .sidebar-overlay { display: none; }
}

/* ── Responsive ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .sidebar { transform: translateX(-100%); }
  .sidebar.open { transform: translateX(0); }
  .sidebar-overlay.open { display: block; }
  .menu-toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
  .main { margin-left: 0; padding: 64px 20px 60px; }
  .barrier-item { flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; }
  .barrier-label { min-width: unset; }
}
</style>
</head>

<!-- Main -->
<div class="layout">
<main class="main">

<!-- Cover -->
<section class="cover-section" id="cover">
  <div class="cover-border"></div>
  <p class="chapter-eyebrow" style="margin-bottom:8px">A Transformative Workbook</p>
  <h1 class="cover-title">GIVE YOURSELF</h1>
  <div class="cover-grace">Grace</div>
  <div class="cover-rule"></div>
  <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Woman with a full, scattered mind — ready for grace" class="cover-figure">
  <p class="cover-sub">A Workbook for Asking for Help &amp; Living from Abundance</p>
  <p class="cover-tag"><em>Recognizing the power of asking for help is giving yourself Grace.</em></p>
  <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Give Yourself Grace" class="cover-logo">
</section>

<!-- Introduction -->
<section id="intro">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Welcome</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Introduction</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <p>Do you ever push yourself — even when it feels deeply uncomfortable — to make real connections? It's one thing to agree with something in theory, but turning that theory into practice is a whole different ball game. I've come to see that so many people — whether they're entrepreneurs, career professionals, or caregivers — struggle with the same challenge. They're handling their business, making things happen, yet they often choose to struggle alone because they don't want to risk the embarrassment of asking for help, even though, just like me, they need it.</p>
  <p>Some of us are practically drowning in responsibilities, yet we refuse to reach out for a lifeline — or even admit that we need one — as the water keeps rising. Here's the truth: going it alone isn't a badge of honor, and it certainly isn't necessary. When we don't ask for help, we shortchange our families, our communities, our colleagues, ourselves, and the women and girls who look up to us. We miss out on living fully, reaching higher, and serving from a place of abundance.</p>
  <p>So, let's flip the script. Imagine feeling whole instead of stretched thin. Picture operating on a full tank rather than running on fumes, trying to give everything to everyone else without ever asking for anything in return. Everyone — and I mean everyone — deserves support to reach their next level. Think about all the incredible experiences and magic you could create if you just opened yourself up to a little help. It's not just okay to ask for help — it's downright inspiring!</p>
  <div class="intro-quote">"Give yourself Grace — recognizing the power of asking for help is giving yourself Grace. Open up to support and unlock your full potential."</div>
</section>

<li><a href="#ch15"><span class="toc-num">15</span> Give Responsibility: Take Action, Say No and Mean It</a></li>

<!-- All 15 Chapters -->

<section class="chapter" id="ch1">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 1</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">H.E.L.P</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <h3 class="section-h2">H — Having it all doesn't mean doing it all alone.</h3><p>The most powerful, successful people in the world know this secret: don't try to do it all by yourself. They understand that asking for help isn't a sign of weakness — it's a smart strategy for success. Trying to juggle everything on your own can be exhausting and overwhelming. But when you reach out for support, you're not just lightening your load — you're also inviting fresh perspectives, new ideas, and valuable resources into your life.</p><p>Whether you're an entrepreneur, a career professional, or a caregiver, remember that it's okay to ask for help. In fact, it's more than okay — it's inspiring. Imagine what you could achieve with a little backup. You'd be operating from a place of strength and abundance, rather than simply trying to get by on fumes.</p><h3 class="section-h2">E — Ask Empowering Questions.</h3><p>Instead of beating yourself up with "Why am I so stupid?" or "Why don't I just give up?" — try asking: "What am I missing?" "What can I learn from this moment?" or "How can I get support for this?" Approach empowering questions with enthusiasm rather than dread. Be open to the answers — you might be surprised by what you discover!</p><h3 class="section-h2">L — Let Go of the "How."</h3><p>Let go of your expectations about how the support you need will come to you. Release those expectations and allow support to show up in its own way. You don't have to control the "how." Trust that it will come together as it should, and stay open to the surprises along the way.</p><h3 class="section-h2">P — Believe in the Possibilities.</h3><p>You've got to believe that abundant support is out there and that it will come your way. Your thoughts are far more powerful than you might realize. Ditch those limiting beliefs and embrace "possibility thinking." Open yourself up, make room for the support you need, and trust that it's on its way. Be ready to welcome it when it arrives!</p>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 1 · Deliberations</span>

<section class="chapter" id="ch2">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 2</span>

  </div>

    <p>For each category below, jot down your specific goal and your "big-leap" goal — a goal that pushes you beyond your comfort zone. Most of us play it safe when setting goals. This is your chance to write down a goal that feels almost impossible to achieve. Does it make you squirm just thinking about it? Perfect — that's the one. Write it down.</p><h3 class="section-h2">Before You Begin, Remember:</h3><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Be Specific</strong><p>Being specific turns a dream into an objective. How much money? By when? Being clear and precise keeps you accountable.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Let Go of the "How"</strong><p>Your "what" and your "why" are essential. Don't stress about the "how" right now — trust that the path will unfold as you boldly move forward.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Set Your Intention</strong><p>What do you want to feel or experience when you achieve this dream? Your intention acts like a compass, keeping you grounded when things get tough.</p></div></div><h3 class="section-h2">Your Goals</h3><div class="note-box">

<section class="chapter" id="ch3">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 3</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">I Have the Power to Do It All</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>Feeling like you can do it all typically shows up in four ways. Recognizing which pattern applies to you is the first step toward meaningful change.</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Defiant</strong><p>You respond with a confident "I got it!" to prove you're not weak or incapable. This ego-driven reaction often stems from a belief that no one else can do the task as well as you can.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Defensive</strong><p>Whether you truly believe you can handle it or not, you insist you have it covered because you need to prove something — to yourself or to others. Feeling like you must do everything becomes a shield against potential criticism.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Defeated</strong><p>You're exhausted, but you still say "I have it," because you feel like no one else will step up if you don't. You've become the default person who handles everything — whether you want to or not.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Realizing You Can't Do It All</strong><p>Thinking you can handle everything on your own often leads to the realization that you simply can't. Many people struggle with accepting help and refuse it even when it's offered. By insisting on doing everything ourselves, we miss opportunities to connect with others and show up at our very best. Give yourself some grace.</p></div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 3 · Deliberations</span>

<section class="chapter" id="ch4">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 4</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Act, Set Priorities, and Maximize</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <h3 class="section-h2">How Not to Feel Overwhelmed</h3><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Make a List of Your Activities — and Check It Twice</strong><p>Start by jotting down all the activities you do every week. Then organize by priority, from most important to least. Is it genuinely a priority, or something you continue out of habit? If your activities don't align with your true priorities, it's time to trim the list.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Cull Your Activities</strong><p>As you review your activities and compare them to your priorities, be honest about whether they align. Optimize your time by cutting activities that don't serve your goals. Regularly ask: "Is this still in line with my priorities?"</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Ask for Help</strong><p>After trimming your list, it's time to ask for help. Identify tasks to eliminate or delegate, and don't be afraid to ask your partner for assistance, hire someone, or delegate to family members. Take small steps and celebrate the little wins along the way.</p></div></div><h3 class="section-h2">My Weekly Activity List</h3><p>List everything you do in a typical week, then mark each as: Priority (P) / Review (R) / Eliminate (E).</p><div class="note-box">

<section class="chapter" id="ch5">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 5</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Fall Back — You Don't Have to Do It All</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <h3 class="section-h2">Embrace the Value of Stepping Back and Asking for Support</h3><p>If you're struggling to figure out why you can't do it all, you're not alone. Many people face common barriers that prevent them from accepting support, even when it's offered:</p><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Mindset</span><p>Your belief system might convince you that asking for help makes you look weak or incapable, undermining your sense of independence.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Past Experience</span><p>Previous experiences may have led you to believe that relying on others results in disappointment, making you wary of seeking assistance.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Fear of Missing Out</span><p>You might worry that if you delegate tasks, you'll miss out on important opportunities or experiences.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Pride and Independence</span><p>You might feel that asking for help makes you look weak, undermining your self-reliance.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Fear of Judgment</span><p>You could be worried about how others will perceive you if you admit you need assistance.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Trust Issues</span><p>You might believe that no one else can do the task as well as you can, leading to a reluctance to delegate.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Control</span><p>Letting go of control can be hard. You might fear that things won't be done to your standards if someone else takes over.</p></div><div class="barrier-item"><span class="barrier-label">Habit</span><p>Sometimes it's simply habit. You're used to doing everything yourself and haven't yet practiced the art of asking for and accepting help.</p></div><p>By understanding these common factors, you can begin to overcome them and make room for the support you need. Embrace the courage to step back and don't be afraid to ask for it.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 5 · Deliberations</span>
      <h3 class="deli-title">FALL BACK — YOU DON'T HAVE TO DO IT ALL</h3>
      <div class="slate-rule"></div>
    </div>

  </div>

</div><div class="question-block">
  <div class="question-header">
    <span class="question-label">How Much Control Do You Need?</span>
    <p class="question-prompt">Letting go of control can be challenging. How can you practice releasing some control and trusting others to meet your standards?</p>

    <span class="question-label">Is Habit Keeping You from Accepting Help?</span>
    <p class="question-prompt">Are you simply used to doing everything yourself? What small steps can you take to break this habit and start practicing the art of asking for and accepting help?</p>

<section class="chapter" id="ch6">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 6</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Learn the Language of Asking</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <h3 class="section-h2">The Courage and Art of Being Vulnerable</h3><p>Being vulnerable isn't easy — it takes real courage, practice, and trust. Sharing your inner thoughts, feelings, desires, and insecurities should be done in an environment where you feel safe. Before you open up, consider:</p><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>Is this a space that will honor you and your experience?</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>Will you feel supported here?</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>If there is any pushback, do you trust that the conversation will remain respectful and productive?</p></div><h3 class="section-h2">Share Your Scars, Not Your Wounds</h3><p>It's perfectly okay to share your scars rather than your open wounds. When you choose to share your scars, you're talking about experiences you've already healed from — and that kind of sharing offers hope to others while celebrating your own resilience and growth.</p><h3 class="section-h2">Find Your Vulnerability Warriors</h3><p>Take a moment to identify three people you can rely on for support — your vulnerability warriors. These are people who are brave enough to share with you and loving enough to listen without judgment.</p><div class="note-box">
  <label class="note-box-label" for="ch6_nb9">My Three Vulnerability Warriors:</label>

<section class="chapter" id="ch7">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 7</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Remove Your Mask: Take Action and Be Yourself</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>The mask is the façade you use to hide your true feelings and who you really are from the outside world. Here are steps to help you start removing your mask and embracing your authentic self:</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Turn It Off</strong><p>Give yourself permission to not be "on" all the time. Step back and step away. Life will continue even when you take a moment for yourself.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Do Something Intentional</strong><p>Once you give yourself permission, be intentional about addressing your pain. Call a therapist, make an appointment, or plan a vacation. Do something specific to break the pattern — and do it on purpose.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Tap Into a Higher Power</strong><p>Keep your spirit open to guidance from God or your higher power. Stay open, and you will receive signals telling you when you need a break, when to slow down, or when to stop.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Reflect and Journal</strong><p>Take time to reflect on your feelings and experiences. Writing in a journal can help you process your emotions and understand what's behind the mask.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">5</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Find Your Support System</strong><p>Surround yourself with people who accept you for who you are — your vulnerability warriors.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">6</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Practice Self-Compassion</strong><p>Be kind to yourself. It's okay to have flaws and to make mistakes. Treat yourself with the same kindness you would offer a close friend.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">7</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Set Boundaries</strong><p>Learn to say no and set boundaries that protect your time and energy. It's okay to prioritize your own needs.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">8</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Celebrate Small Wins</strong><p>Acknowledge and celebrate your progress, no matter how small. Each step toward being more authentic is a victory worth recognizing.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">9</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Stay Open to Growth</strong><p>Removing the mask is a process, not an overnight change. Each day is an opportunity to be a little more true to yourself.</p></div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 7 · Deliberations</span>

<section class="chapter" id="ch8">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 8</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Take Action: Come Up with a Reinvention Plan</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>At some point, everyone faces the need to reinvent themselves — due to relocation, job changes, health challenges, or personal growth. Having a solid reinvention strategy is crucial. Here are steps to help you create your own plan:</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Secure Your Financial Foundation</strong><p>It's essential to have savings equivalent to at least one year's salary to support your transition to the next phase of life.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Prepare for Change</strong><p>Even if you've been with one company for decades and feel secure, having a reinvention plan is wise. Today's career landscape is unpredictable.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Embrace Side Hustles</strong><p>Entrepreneurial ventures or additional income streams aren't just for younger generations. Now is the perfect time to explore new business ideas or expand your current offerings.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Commit to Lifelong Learning</strong><p>Staying engaged with new developments is crucial. Embrace the mindset of a lifelong learner.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">5</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Consult Your "Kitchen Cabinet"</strong><p>Unsure about your next steps? Gather a diverse group of trusted friends from different stages of your life for insights and honest conversation.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">6</span><div class="step-body"><strong>You Define Your Journey</strong><p>Transitioning to a new life chapter means letting go of old identities. Remember, it's your decision when to move forward — no one else's.</p></div></div>
  </div>

    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>When crafting your personal and professional network, it's essential to both cultivate existing relationships and attract new, high-quality connections. Here's how to envision your ideal contacts:</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Describe Your Ideal Contacts</strong><p>Visualize individuals who resonate with your values, ambitions, and energy. Consider traits like their personality, demeanor, and communication style.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Presentation</strong><p>Imagine how they present themselves professionally — both in appearance and in how they carry themselves.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Age Range</strong><p>Specify the age group that aligns with your goals and industry.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Occupation or Business</strong><p>Define their profession or business type that complements your interests or offers potential collaboration.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">5</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Shared Interests</strong><p>List their hobbies, passions, and activities that you share or find intriguing.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">6</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Synergy</strong><p>Determine how your strengths and theirs can complement each other to enhance mutual success.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">7</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Their Needs and Challenges</strong><p>Understand the pain points or challenges your skills or services can address effectively.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">8</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Support and Value</strong><p>Envision how you can best support them or provide value. What unique contributions can you offer?</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">9</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Mutual Appreciation</strong><p>Reflect on what they would appreciate most about collaborating with you — and vice versa.</p></div></div><p>Remember: your ideal contact profile may evolve over time. Stay open to adjustments and release relationships that no longer serve your journey.</p><div class="note-box">

<section class="chapter" id="ch10">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 10</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Seek Wise Counsel: Pause in the Midst of a Crisis</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>During challenging times, when uncertainty rattles your footing, seeking guidance from experienced mentors or advisors with a calm demeanor and clear perspective can be invaluable. Here are four practices to help you respond with clarity:</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Center Yourself with Deep Breathing</strong><p>Find a quiet place, plant both feet firmly on the ground, and take slow, deep breaths. Inhale for four counts, hold for four, exhale slowly for six counts, and hold for two. Visualize breathing in light, strength, and positivity — and exhaling tension, anxiety, and limiting beliefs.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Pause Before Acting</strong><p>Resist the urge to react immediately. Allow yourself time — several hours or ideally overnight — to let your emotions settle. The goal is to create space between your feelings and the event that shook your world. Remember: feel first, then problem-solve.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Avoid Hasty Decisions</strong><p>Instead of hastily giving up or discarding options, take time to breathe and step back. Avoid making decisions you might regret later by gaining perspective once your emotions have stabilized.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Seek Wise Counsel</strong><p>Turn to someone who offers level-headed advice tailored to your needs. Consider reaching out to a coach or professional counselor who understands your story, challenges, triggers, and aspirations.</p></div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 10 · Deliberations</span>

<section class="chapter" id="ch11">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 11</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">View Feedback as a Gift: Curate Your Circle of Influence</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>Reflect on how you process feedback from trusted sources. Do you find yourself dwelling on bruised pride, or do you choose to reflect and consider how you can improve? Being open to constructive feedback can significantly propel your growth. Your circle of influence typically consists of three key layers:</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Inner Circle</strong><p>Your inner circle consists of people who aren't afraid to give you honest feedback, even when it's tough to hear. They know you well and genuinely want to see you succeed.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Mentor Circle</strong><p>Your mentors are seasoned experts in their respective fields. Their feedback comes from a place of deep knowledge and trustworthiness. They offer guidance that can shape your path with wisdom and experience.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Distant Friends Circle</strong><p>These are friends you consider part of your broader social network, though not your closest companions. They bring strengths and perspectives different from your own, fostering a mutually beneficial relationship.</p></div></div><p>Each circle plays a unique role. Be intentional about who you invite into each layer, and honor the feedback you receive as a gift — even when it's hard to hear.</p><h3 class="section-h2">My Circle of Influence</h3><div class="note-box">

<section class="chapter" id="ch12">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 12</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Show Up for Yourself: Give Yourself Grace</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>One of the most powerful things you can do is show up for yourself — fully, intentionally, and with compassion. Giving yourself grace isn't passive; it's an active, courageous choice.</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Create a Resource List</strong><p>Create a list of at least ten resources, organizations, tools, and individuals that can help you achieve your goals. Don't overthink it; just jot them down.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Set a Deadline and Reach Out</strong><p>Once you have your list, set a clear deadline to start reaching out. Take proactive steps toward connecting and utilizing these opportunities to move forward.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Be Present for Yourself</strong><p>Practice being present in your own life. This means noticing when you're running on empty, when you need rest, and when you need to ask for support — without guilt.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Embrace Grace Daily</strong><p>Grace is not a one-time gift — it's a daily practice. Each morning, remind yourself that you are enough. Each evening, acknowledge what you've done well, even in the smallest ways.</p></div></div><h3 class="section-h2">My Resource Brainstorm List</h3><p>List at least 10 resources, organizations, tools, or people who can help you move forward:</p><div class="numlist"><div class="numlist-row"><span class="numlist-n">1.</span><input type="text" id="ch12_nl7_1" name="ch12_nl7_1" class="numlist-input" placeholder=""></div>

<section class="chapter" id="ch13">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 13</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Let People Show Up for You</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>Learning to welcome support from others is one of the most transformative things you can do for yourself — and for those around you. Here's how to open the door and let people in:</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Own It</strong><p>You have to embrace what you want, and that might be exactly why it feels scary. Start by saying: "This is what I want. This is what I need." Stand firmly in that. Own your desires and needs without shame or blame.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Just Make the Ask</strong><p>It might sound simple, but you've got to push yourself to do it. You won't want to, and all that negative self-talk will try to hold you back. Take action before the fearful part of your mind takes over.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Be Specific</strong><p>People love details, so be clear about what you're asking for. Explain what you've done so far, what you're trying to achieve, and the roadblocks you're facing.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Be Willing to Negotiate</strong><p>Sometimes you might not be able to give 100%, but maybe you can offer 80%. Identify the bare minimums and be ready to discuss and compromise.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">5</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Have Your Non-Negotiables</strong><p>While negotiating is essential, knowing your non-negotiables is just as important. This clarity helps you recognize what's broken and what can be fixed on a healthy foundation.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">6</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Know That You Deserve Support</strong><p>Many people don't ask for help because, deep down, they don't feel like they deserve it. Remember your why — especially if it goes beyond yourself. The sense of deserving will follow.</p></div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 13 · Deliberations</span>

<section class="chapter" id="ch14">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 14</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Embrace a Little Grace: Take Action and Let It Go</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>We often fear outside judgment, but we can be our own harshest critics — saying things to ourselves that we wouldn't dream of saying to others. When you let go of preconceived notions about what support should look like, you'll find that it can appear in the most surprising ways. Give yourself grace and allow that support in.</p><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">1</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Get Over Perfection</strong><p>Embracing vulnerability is key — it's okay to mess up, feel angry, or be sad. Allowing yourself to acknowledge and address your emotions is not weakness; it's wisdom.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">2</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Forget About Perfect Balance</strong><p>There's no such thing as perfect work-life balance — it's more about living in harmony with all parts of your life. Rather than striving for an elusive balance, embrace the ebb and flow of different aspects of your life.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">3</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Go Easy on Yourself</strong><p>No one gets everything right all the time. When things don't go as planned, resist the urge to spiral into shame and guilt. Give yourself a little grace instead.</p></div></div><div class="step-item"><span class="step-num">4</span><div class="step-body"><strong>Be True to Yourself</strong><p>A lot of stress and guilt stems from trying to maintain a perfect image for others. Break free from this by embracing your real, authentic self. Being authentic not only liberates us, but also connects us with others through shared experiences.</p></div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 14 · Deliberations</span>
      <h3 class="deli-title">EMBRACE A LITTLE GRACE: TAKE ACTION AND LET IT GO</h3>
      <div class="slate-rule"></div>
    </div>

  </div>

<section class="chapter" id="ch15">
  <div class="chapter-header">
    <span class="chapter-eyebrow">Chapter 15</span>
    <h2 class="chapter-title">Give Responsibility: Take Action, Say No and Mean It</h2>
    <div class="amber-rule"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="chapter-content">
    <p>Practice embracing your "no." It doesn't have to be harsh or unkind, but it should be firm and genuine. You don't have to say yes to every request that comes your way. It's important to support yourself by using your "no" to uphold your boundaries.</p><p>Saying "yes" when you lack the time, energy, or expertise can end up wasting resources for both parties. Being truthful is a service to yourself and others.</p><p>When you say "yes" to something out of obligation or guilt — rather than genuine enthusiasm — remember that you're also saying "no" to many other opportunities that could truly inspire you.</p><h3 class="section-h2">Situations Where It's Perfectly Okay to Say No:</h3><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When you lack the time, energy, or expertise to do it well.</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When it doesn't align with your current priorities or goals.</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When it conflicts with your values or non-negotiables.</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When you're already at capacity and adding more would lead to burnout.</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When the opportunity doesn't excite or inspire you.</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When your participation would be out of obligation rather than genuine desire.</p></div><div class="bullet-item"><span class="bullet-dot">•</span><p>When saying yes would require you to say no to something more important.</p></div><p>Don't let the fear of missing out push you into saying "yes" when "no" is what you truly need.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="deliberations-section">
    <div class="deli-header">
      <span class="deli-eyebrow">Chapter 15 · Deliberations</span>
      <h3 class="deli-title">GIVE RESPONSIBILITY: TAKE ACTION, SAY NO AND MEAN IT</h3>
      <div class="slate-rule"></div>
    </div>

  <div class="question-header">
    <span class="question-label">Reflect on Your Boundaries</span>
    <p class="question-prompt">How do you currently establish and communicate your boundaries, especially when it comes to saying "no" to requests that don't align with your priorities?</p>
  </div>
  <textarea id="ch15_q1" name="ch15_q1" class="response-area" rows="5" placeholder="Write your response here..."></textarea>

  </div>

  </div>
  <textarea id="ch15_q4" name="ch15_q4" class="response-area" rows="5" placeholder="Write your response here..."></textarea>
</div><div class="question-block">
  <div class="question-header">
    <span class="question-label">Practice Assertiveness</span>

<!-- Notes pages -->
<section class="chapter" id="notes"><div class="chapter-header"><span class="chapter-eyebrow">Pages for Reflection</span><h2 class="chapter-title">My Notes</h2><div class="amber-rule"></div></div><div class="notes-page">
  <div class="notes-page-header">
    <span class="notes-page-num">Page 1 of 5</span>
    <p class="notes-page-sub">Use this space freely — thoughts, reflections, intentions, or whatever is on your mind.</p>
  </div>
  <textarea name="notes_1" class="notes-area" rows="20" placeholder="Your notes..."></textarea>
</div><div class="notes-page">
  <div class="notes-page-header">
    <span class="notes-page-num">Page 2 of 5</span>
    <p class="notes-page-sub">Use this space freely — thoughts, reflections, intentions, or whatever is on your mind.</p>
  </div>
  <textarea name="notes_2" class="notes-area" rows="20" placeholder="Your notes..."></textarea>
</div><div class="notes-page">
  <div class="notes-page-header">
    <span class="notes-page-num">Page 3 of 5</span>
    <p class="notes-page-sub">Use this space freely — thoughts, reflections, intentions, or whatever is on your mind.</p>
  </div>
  <textarea name="notes_3" class="notes-area" rows="20" placeholder="Your notes..."></textarea>
</div><div class="notes-page">
  <div class="notes-page-header">
    <span class="notes-page-num">Page 4 of 5</span>
    <p class="notes-page-sub">Use this space freely — thoughts, reflections, intentions, or whatever is on your mind.</p>
  </div>
  <textarea name="notes_4" class="notes-area" rows="20" placeholder="Your notes..."></textarea>
</div><div class="notes-page">
  <div class="notes-page-header">
    <span class="notes-page-num">Page 5 of 5</span>
    <p class="notes-page-sub">Use this space freely — thoughts, reflections, intentions, or whatever is on your mind.</p>
  </div>
  <textarea name="notes_5" class="notes-area" rows="20" placeholder="Your notes..."></textarea>
</div></section>

</main>
</div>

<script>
// ── Sidebar toggle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
const btn      = document.getElementById('menuBtn');
const sidebar  = document.getElementById('sidebar');
const overlay  = document.getElementById('overlay');

btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
  sidebar.classList.toggle('open');
  overlay.classList.toggle('open');
});
overlay.addEventListener('click', () => {
  sidebar.classList.remove('open');
  overlay.classList.remove('open');
});

// ── Active link on scroll ──────────────────────────────────────────
const sections = document.querySelectorAll('[id]');
const navLinks = document.querySelectorAll('.sidebar-nav a');

const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
  entries.forEach(e => {
    if (e.isIntersecting) {
      navLinks.forEach(a => a.classList.remove('active'));
      const link = document.querySelector(`.sidebar-nav a[href="#${e.target.id}"]`);
      if (link) link.classList.add('active');
    }
  });
}, { rootMargin: '-20% 0px -70% 0px' });

sections.forEach(s => observer.observe(s));

// ── Progress tracking ──────────────────────────────────────────────
const allFields = document.querySelectorAll('textarea, input[type="text"]');
const fill      = document.getElementById('progressFill');
const pct       = document.getElementById('progressPct');

function updateProgress() {
  let filled = 0;
  allFields.forEach(f => { if (f.value.trim().length > 0) filled++; });
  const percent = allFields.length ? Math.round((filled / allFields.length) * 100) : 0;
  fill.style.width = percent + '%';
  pct.textContent  = percent + '% complete';
}

allFields.forEach(f => f.addEventListener('input', updateProgress));
updateProgress();

// ── Auto-save to localStorage ──────────────────────────────────────
function saveAll() {
  allFields.forEach(f => { if (f.id || f.name) localStorage.setItem('gyg_' + (f.id || f.name), f.value); });
}

function loadAll() {
  allFields.forEach(f => {
    const key = 'gyg_' + (f.id || f.name);
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(key);
    if (saved) f.value = saved;
  });
  updateProgress();
}

allFields.forEach(f => f.addEventListener('input', saveAll));
loadAll();

// ── Smooth scroll sidebar links ────────────────────────────────────
navLinks.forEach(a => {
  a.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const target = document.querySelector(a.getAttribute('href'));
    if (target) target.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });
    sidebar.classList.remove('open');
    overlay.classList.remove('open');
  });
});
</script>
</body>
</html>
